ModifyDamageAdditive.maps_to: modify_damage_additive (strike_dummy.py:23-32), dispatched by HookSystem.modify_damage_additive (hooks.py:52-64) from DamageCmd.deal (cmds.py:56-57)
ModifyDamageAdditive.issue: **replaces the record's own "WHAT REMAINS" framing.** The record described this as an open residual (dealer-only check, no card-ownership consult). Executed confirmation: `StrikeDummy.cs:33-36` declines the bonus only when BOTH `dealer != Owner.Creature` AND `cardSource.Owner != Owner` are true — either disjunct alone keeps the bonus. The sim has **no enemy-owned `Card`** anywhere (no `card.owner` attribute exists at all; grepped, confirmed by reading `cards/base.py`) — every card in this scope belongs to the player. So `cardSource.Owner == Owner` (`self.player`) always holds, the second disjunct is never true, the AND can never be satisfied, and **C# would never decline this bonus on dealer grounds at all** — the `dealer is self.player` guard the sim had was simply wrong, not a narrower-but-safe stand-in. Fixed by dropping the dealer check entirely (`relics/strike_dummy.py`): the bonus now applies whenever `is_powered_attack(props)` and the card is Strike-tagged, regardless of `dealer`. Re-confirmed by census (`test_r13_relic1.py::test_strike_tagged_cards_all_deal_damage_with_the_player_as_dealer`, unmodified, still green) that no currently-ported Strike-tagged card ever calls `DamageCmd.deal` with a non-player dealer — so this fix changes nothing observable in today's ported content (hence `live: false`) but removes an incorrect guard that would have silently broken the first future effect routing card damage through a different dealer (a delegated or reflected hit). Pinned by `test_strike_dummy_grants_bonus_with_no_dealer`. **Breaks a stale pre-existing test, not owned by this lane's footprint:** `test/test_r13_relic1.py::test_strike_dummy_misses_a_null_dealer_strike` (line 325-335) asserts the OLD, now-superseded behaviour (`with_none == base`, commented "dormant divergence: C# would still add 3" — that comment was actually correctly diagnosing the gap but the test asserted the sim's wrong behaviour rather than the C#-correct one). It now fails (`7 == 6` become `9 == 6`... concretely `with_none` is now `base + 3`, not `base`). **The controller should update it** — replace the final assertion with `assert with_none == base + 3 # StrikeDummy.EXTRA_DAMAGE -- card ownership always == player in this sim, so dealer no longer gates it` (and update the docstring/comment above the class at `test_r13_relic1.py:257-262`, which documents the now-stale round-13 "dormancy re-confirmed" verdict for G2 specifically).

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): C# grants the +3 when EITHER the dealer is the owner's creature OR the Strike card BELONGS to the owner; the port requires the dealer
guards.issue: MECHANISM: StrikeDummy.cs:33-36 is `if (dealer != base.Owner.Creature && cardSource.Owner != base.Owner) return 0m;` -- a conjunction of negatives, so either clause alone suffices. strike_dummy.py:30 requires `dealer is self.player` and never consults the card's owner (the sim's Card has no owner concept in this hook's signature). Two sub-cases follow. (a) A player-owned Strike-tagged card whose damage is dealt with a dealer that is not the player -- C# pays, the sim does not. (b) In multiplayer, another player's Strike dealt BY this owner's creature -- waived under the shared contract's multiplayer exclusion. REACHABILITY of (a) (DORMANT, executed census -- b15-censuses): the ported Strike-tagged cards are exactly eight (ashen_strike, perfected_strike, pommel_strike, seeker_strike, setup_strike, strike, twin_strike, ultimate_strike) and ALL EIGHT pass `dealer=ctx.player` to DamageCmd.deal -- zero exceptions -- so no ported play can reach the branch. EXECUTED demonstration of the divergence with a synthetic call (b15-misc): `DamageCmd.deal(..., 6, dealer=None, card=make_card('strike'), props=DamageProps.CARD)` deals 6 in the sim where C# deals 9. What makes it live: porting any effect that re-deals a player's Strike-tagged card's damage from another creature (a player-side summon, a 'the enemy plays your card' effect) or that passes dealer=None on a card attack.

This is PROMPT.md bug class 24 -- a docstring that misdescribes the PORT and would point a later reader at a false gap -- so the verdict is on the CODE, which is correct, and the comment is flagged rather than filed. EXECUTED (b15-misc): a Strike gets 6 -> 9, a Bash gets 6 -> 6, and an UNPOWERED Strike gets 6 -> 6.

guards.what: N3: the RETURN CONVENTION -- C# returns 0m to decline, and the sim's dispatcher SUMS listener returns
guards.rationale: Hook.ModifyDamageInternal accumulates `num += num2` over the listeners and records each non-zero contributor in its out-modifiers list (Hook.cs:2515-2524); hooks.py:60-64 sums the same way. strike_dummy.py:32 returns 0 on the decline path, matching StrikeDummy.cs's four `return 0m` bails, so declining adds nothing on either side. The one thing C#'s dispatcher carries that the sim's does not is membership of the modifiers list (which drives Hook.AfterModifyingDamageAmount); Strike Dummy implements no AfterModifyingDamageAmount, so it cannot observe that -- recorded because audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json step 38 owns the general case.
